Use One-Way ANOVA to determine whether the population means of two or more groups differ. If the ANOVA finds that at least one group is different, perform a comparisons analysis to identify pairs of groups that are significantly different. The input data can be a stack of continuous responses and corresponding a categorical factor column, or separated columns of continuous samples. [Click HELP for more info.]

The two-way ANOVA compares the mean differences between groups that have been split on two independent variables (called factors). Use a two-way ANOVA when you want to know how two independent categorical variables (factors), in combination, affect a dependent variable (response). [Click HELP for more info.]

Use Cross Tabulation and Chi-Square analysis when your data is categorized by two categorical variables. Input the categorical data with two columns. Use a summarized table when the rows and columns contain total counts for each cross-category. [Click HELP for more info.]

Gage R&R (Repeatability and Reproducibility) is a statistical tool used to assess measurement system reliability, evaluating both equipment precision and operator consistency. This study requires a balanced design where all operators measure all parts, with each part measured an equal number of times. The study can be conducted with one or multiple operators. Various algorithms are available, aligning with different commercial software. [Click HELP for more info.]

Nested Gage R&R is used when parts cannot be measured by multiple operators, typically in destructive testing. Each part is measured by a single operator, potentially multiple times, with the requirement that all operators measure an equal number of parts to ensure statistical balance and reliability of the measurement system variation analysis. [Click HELP for more info.]

Process capability measurement is a statistical method used to evaluate how well a manufacturing process can produce parts within specified limits consistently. The main indices used for this measurement are Cp, Cpk, Pp, and Ppk. The function is to evaluate data without subgrouping, for example, lot, machine, etc.. Use the function of 'Cpk with subgroups' for subgrouped data instead. [Click HELP for more info.]
Show within sigma of moving average of neighbor observations.

Process capability measurement is a statistical method used to evaluate how well a manufacturing process can produce parts within specified limits consistently. The function requires samples having subgroups, like lot, shift, equipment etc.. Use the function of 'Process Capability' for data without subgroups instead. [Click HELP for more info.]

A tolerance interval defines the upper and/or lower bounds within which a certain percent of the process output falls with a stated confidence. Computes an interval that contains at least the specified proportion of the population with (1-alpha) confidence, assuming Normal Distribution. [Click HELP for more info.]

An I/MR control chart is a process control tool designed for situations where data is collected one observation at a time, without traditional subgrouping. Instead, it uses a moving window to group neighboring data points into pseudo subgroups. To use the chart, select the 'value' as the process measurement to be controlled, and specify the moving range to determine how many neighboring points are included in each pseudo subgroup. [Click HELP for more info.]

An Individuals control chart is a process control tool designed for situations where data is collected one observation at a time, without traditional subgrouping. This function will solely draw the control chart with individual observations without a moving range control chart. To use the chart, select the 'value' as the process measurement to be controlled. [Click HELP for more info.]

An MR control chart is a process control tool designed for situations where data is collected one observation at a time, without traditional subgrouping. It uses a moving window to group neighboring data points into pseudo subgroups. To use the chart, select the 'value' as the process measurement to be controlled, and specify the moving range to determine how many neighboring points are included in each pseudo subgroup. [Click HELP for more info.]

A fitted distribution is a theoretical distribution calculated using parameter estimates derived from a sample that you enter. This dialog can help to find the most suitable distribution to the sample. If plotting required, please use Plots>Histogram & Dist. Fit, however which can't compare across distributions.
